insurance: A contract under which the insurer pays money when an insured event occurs
A policy sets out what you are insured against, for what amount and under what conditions a payout will be made.
What is a deductible in insurance?
The part of the damage you cover yourself
The name of an insurance company
Part of the loss stays with you.
A deductible lowers the policy price: you pay small losses yourself, the insurer pays large ones.
Your liability to other parties in an accident
Motor liability insurance compensates victims if you are at fault. Your own car is protected by voluntary comprehensive insurance.
A payout on an insured event
A state award to the insurer
The amount you pay for the policy
The premium is your payment for protection, and the insurance payout is the money you receive when an insured event occurs.
What is most important to check in an insurance contract?
The list of insured events and exclusions
When they pay and when they do not.
The worst thing is to find out after an incident that your case is among the exclusions. Read this section before buying.
Can you cancel voluntary insurance taken out together with a loan?
Yes, during the cooling-off period, with a refund
Only when the loan is closed
There is time to change your mind.
Voluntary insurance can usually be returned within the cooling-off period. But if the contract provides for it, the bank may raise the rate.
Why insure a home if it is not mortgaged?
So that major damage does not wipe out your savings
A fire or flood can cost more than all your savings. A policy shifts this risk to the insurer for a small fee.
What is liability insurance toward neighbors?
A policy for the management company
A policy that pays for neighbors' repairs if you flood them
It is inexpensive, while repairing several apartments can cost hundreds of thousands.
When does life insurance make the most sense?
When loved ones depend on your income
When you have no children and no debts
Who would suffer without your income?
If your family or mortgage relies on your income, life insurance protects loved ones from financial disaster.
Why is investment life insurance often criticized?
High hidden fees and penalties for early exit
The guaranteed return is too high
A complex product with many fees.
Returns are often eaten by fees, and early exit returns less than invested. It is important to read the terms.
An apartment worth 4 million ₽ is insured for 2 million ₽, the damage is 1 million ₽, and the payout is proportional. How much will be paid?
With underinsurance the payout is often proportional: 2 / 4 = 50% of the damage. Check this clause in the contract.
The insurer's risk assessment before signing a contract
Based on underwriting, the insurer decides whether to insure and at what price. Hiding important facts is not allowed, it is grounds to refuse a payout.
pension: Regular payments after the end of working life or on special grounds
A pension is granted for age, disability or loss of a breadwinner. Its size depends on work record and earnings.
What mainly funds a state old-age pension?
Social insurance contributions paid by the employer for the employee
The employer pays contributions on your official salary. They form your pension rights.
Why does an official salary matter for your future pension?
It is higher than an unofficial one
Contributions are paid on it, forming pension rights
No contributions are paid on salary "in an envelope", and in old age that work record and earnings will not count.
What is a non-state pension fund?
A branch of the social fund
An organization that saves and invests pension money
A non-state pension fund manages pension savings and voluntary contributions, investing them under the regulator's rules.
Why should you not rely only on the state pension?
It is usually much lower than your usual income
It is paid only to men
A pension usually replaces only part of previous earnings, so personal retirement savings are a sensible safeguard.
Where can you find your pension points and work record (in Russia)?
In the Social Fund personal account or on Gosuslugi
They show your work record, points and employer contributions. It is better to find errors now than when the pension is assigned.
What does starting retirement savings early give you?
More time for compound interest to work
5,000 ₽ a month at 8% from age 25 to 60 grows to about 11.5 million ₽, but from 45 only to 1.7 million ₽.
What is the long-term savings program (in Russia)?
A deposit at the central bank
Voluntary savings via a non-state pension fund with state co-financing
Contributions can be topped up with state co-financing and a tax deduction within the program's terms. Check the terms on official resources.
Raising the pension in line with price growth
Indexation is meant to preserve the pension's purchasing power as prices rise.
The ratio of the pension to previous earnings
The number of pensioners per worker
What share of the salary the pension replaces.
If the salary is 60,000 ₽ and the pension is 24,000 ₽, the replacement rate is 40%. The lower it is, the more important personal savings are.
Why does an aging population put pressure on a pay-as-you-go pension system?
There are fewer workers per pensioner
In a pay-as-you-go system workers pay for current pensioners. When there are fewer workers, the burden on each grows.
What is more effective for a pension over 30 years, all else equal?
Spending everything and saving only in the last 5 years
Regular contributions with reinvestment let compound interest work for decades, which beats one-off efforts at the end.
history: What was used as money before coins?
Commodity money was inconvenient: it spoiled and was hard to divide. Metal coins solved these problems.
Exchanging goods for goods without money
Barter requires a coincidence of wants: you need someone who wants what you have and offers what you need. Money removes this problem.
Where did paper money first appear?
Paper money appeared in China around the 7th–11th centuries and came into mass use under the Song dynasty.
Where does the word "ruble" come from, according to one version?
From the name of a river
From "rubit", to chop: a chopped-off piece of a silver ingot
Silver ingots called grivnas were chopped into pieces, and according to one version the chopped-off piece was called a ruble.
A system where money is backed by gold and exchanged for it at a fixed rate
Under the gold standard, paper money could be exchanged for a set amount of gold.
Why was the gold standard abandoned?
The amount of money was tied to gold reserves, which made it hard to respond to crises. The system was finally wound down in the 1970s.
Very fast price growth, from 50% a month
Classic examples are Germany in 1923 and Zimbabwe in the 2000s, when prices doubled in days.
Money whose value rests on trust and law
Modern money is fiat: its value is backed by law and trust in the state and the central bank.
Where did the first stock exchange in the modern sense appear?
The 17th-century Amsterdam exchange traded shares of the East India Company, the first widely traded shares.
What caused the "tulip mania" of the 17th century?
Speculative frenzy that detached prices from real value
People bought to resell at a higher price.
It is one of the first recorded financial bubbles: the price was set by expectations of resale, not usefulness.
What did the Great Depression of 1929 mean for depositors?
Mass bank failures without deposit insurance
Thousands of banks went bust and people lost their savings. After that, deposit insurance appeared in the US, and later in many countries.
What is bitcoin from an economist's point of view?
A decentralized digital asset with high volatility
It is not issued by a central bank, and its price swings strongly. For savings it is a high-risk asset.
economy: A sustained rise in the general price level
With inflation, the same amount of money buys fewer goods and services over time.
The amount of money in banks
The value of all goods and services produced in a country over a period
GDP is the main measure of the size of an economy. Its growth means the country produces more.
What happens to the price when demand rises and supply stays the same?
More buyers, the same amount of goods.
Buyers compete for a limited amount of goods, so the price goes up.
When a person wants to work but cannot find a job
The unemployment rate shows the share of job seekers among all economically active people.
How does raising the key rate usually affect inflation?
It restrains it: loans get more expensive, saving pays more
People and companies borrow less and save more, demand falls, and price growth slows.
A rise in the national currency's exchange rate
A fall in the national currency's exchange rate
Imported goods become more expensive, while exporters receive more in national currency.
Why do prices rise if there is much more money but not more goods?
There is more money for the same amount of goods
More money, the same amount of goods.
When the money supply grows faster than production, each unit of money buys less.
An economic downturn: falling output and incomes
Technically, a recession is often defined as two consecutive quarters of falling GDP.
A market with only one seller
A monopolist can inflate prices, so the state regulates such markets and watches over competition.
Fast economic growth with low inflation
High inflation with a stagnant economy
Prices rise while the economy stalls or shrinks. It is hard to fight: anti-inflation measures slow growth even more.
Why is moderate inflation of 2–4% considered normal for developed economies?
It is a central bank mistake
It is a tax on the rich
It encourages spending and investing rather than holding cash
Deflation is dangerous: people put off purchases expecting lower prices, and the economy slows.
People spend more when the value of their assets rises
Growth in the number of millionaires
When apartments or shares rise in price, people feel richer and increase consumption even if their income has not grown.
